results.title: NY Fed finds little change in inflation expectations in July

results.content:
The New York Fed’s Survey of Consumer Expectations for July, released on Aug. 7, shows short-term inflation expectations edged down by 0.1 percentage point while medium and longer-term held steady. Perceptions about the current financial situation improved from a year ago, with a larger share of households reporting a better financial situation compared to those reporting a worse one. Median one-year inflation expectations fell by 0.1 percentage point to 3.6%. Medium-term expectations were unchanged at 3.3%, as were longer-term expectations at 3.0%.

results.title: Conference Board: Consumer Confidence Ticks Down in August

results.content:
## Key Takeaways

1.   The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index final reading fell to 51.7 in August, a 6.3% decrease from July.

2.   The Current Economic Conditions Index fell 5.3% to 51.9, while the Consumer Expectations Index fell 7.0% to 51.5.
3.   Year-ahead inflation expectations decreased from 4.0% from 4.2% in July.
